Panel analysis: "Dev-preview roadmap sequencing/dependency risk"

**Dependency ordering is mostly sound, with one real gap.** Capability-matrix task allocation depending on the harness parity pillar makes sense — you can't measure Codex/Grok/Agy/Muse against each other until each can actually execute equivalent tasks. Brainstorm/plan rigor as a foundational pillar ahead of execution velocity also tracks with this project's own Design→Plan→Build gate and the repeated RCA pattern in memory (LIVE-17, the uncommitted-transaction cascade, #1377) where skipped rigor produced expensive rework. Domain-pack competency and large-swarm deployment correctly sit last — both consume the capability matrix as an input, so sequencing them earlier would mean building on unmeasured ground.

**The blocking risk is the local-model pillar.** Shipping Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B as a *measured* 20% contributor inside a 4-week window is the one pillar with a hard, unamortized integration cost: it needs inference serving stood up, task-routing rules that actually send it real work, and then enough completed+merged samples to produce a defensible "20%" number — not a vibes estimate. Per the Empirical Capability Assessment Policy already governing this project (≥5 merged-job samples before a routing claim is credible), 4 weeks is tight to both integrate a new harness *and* clear the sample bar with real PRs. This is the pillar most likely to slip or get rounded to "nominally wired up, not actually measured" — which would be a silent scope-cut disguised as a shipped pillar.

**Second risk, lower severity:** capability-matrix tokenomics/$-accounting depends on `state.db` consolidation (#1926/Track 3), which per project memory is already a known blocking dependency with scattered shards (gh:#1831) — if that consolidation isn't done before the capability-matrix work starts, the accounting pillar inherits the same blocker.

**Recommendation:** approve the sequencing as drafted, but add an explicit checkpoint at end of week 2 gating the local-model pillar specifically — if Hermes integration hasn't produced ≥5 real merged samples by then, descope it to "integrated, unmeasured" rather than let it silently threaten the 10/31 date for the other six pillars.

**Position: Approve with one conditional** — ship the sequencing as-is, but require a week-2 go/no-go checkpoint on the local-model pillar's sample count before treating "measured 20% contributor" as committed scope for 10/31.

### Panel Review & Recommendation: Revised Dev-Preview Roadmap

#### Analysis & Evaluation
The revised dev-preview roadmap ([2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md)) presents a structured, dependency-rigorous 4-week convergence plan targeting the October 31, 2026 release gate (`gh:#1515`). The plan appropriately prioritizes fundamental platform stability over speculative feature expansion.

**Key Technical Strengths of the Sequencing:**
1. **Strict Foundation-First Ordering (Week 1):** Clearing stale goals, fixing job-status reconciliation Bug A ([gh:#2136](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-10-unpushed-branch-verification-retry.md)), and consolidating `state.db` ([#1926](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md#L38)) eliminates data fragmentation across 11,000+ job shards. This directly unblocks Pillars 3 and 4.
2. **Decoupled Telemetry & Measurement (Weeks 2–3):** Stagging Muse CLI calibration and shipping `synlynk capability report` ([#1993](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md#L46)) *after* database consolidation prevents reporting against corrupted or partial metrics. Empowering Hermes-3-Llama-3.1-8B as a measured 20% contributor relies entirely on this Week 2 capability infrastructure landing cleanly.
3. **Pragmatic Scope Boundaries (Weeks 3–4):** Restricting Pillar 6 to a single reference domain pack and Pillar 7 to a single end-to-end swarm field trial avoids premature framework complexity while validating core mechanisms.

**Identified Blocking Risks:**
* **Critical-Path Bottleneck ([#1926](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md#L38)):** If `state.db` consolidation slips past Week 1, capability reporting ([#1993](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md#L46)), cost inflation resolution ([#1937](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md#L47)), and local model telemetry in Weeks 2–3 will stall instantly.
* **Cost Accounting Drift ([#1937](file:///Users/nikhilsoman/dev/synlynk/.claude/worktrees/live24-job-status-reconciliation-investigation/docs/strategy/2026-10-10-dev-preview-revised-roadmap.md#L47)):** Unadjusted Codex job costs threaten the accuracy of tokenomics and dollar-value allocation metrics.
* **Muse Calibration & Infra Role Validation:** Calibrating Muse across implement/test lanes and validating deploy capability via the Infra role in Week 4 leave little schedule slack for unforeseen harness failures.

#### Position & Final Recommendation
I **APPROVE** the revised 4-week roadmap sequencing and dependency ordering for the 2026-10-31 dev-preview release gate (`gh:#1515`). Approval is subject to strictly holding Week 1 as an uncompromised quality gate—specifically requiring `#1926` `state.db` consolidation and `#2136` Bug A fixes to be fully merged before Week 2 dispatch waves and capability report builds commence.

[model=default; version=codex-cli 0.160.0]

**Assessment:** The dependency ordering is mostly sound. Week 1 puts data consolidation and job-status correctness before relying on dispatch metrics; Week 2 builds capability reporting before using it to route work; Week 3 measures Hermes and onboards one domain pack; Week 4 uses those foundations for a swarm trial and release candidate. Keeping domain-pack breadth and other parked work out of scope also supports the deadline.

**Blocking risk:** The schedule puts several critical-path items into a single first week without concrete completion criteria or contingency. Pillar 3 depends on unfinished #1926 state.db consolidation, while #1993 is still unbuilt. If consolidation slips, capability reporting, Hermes measurement, and evidence-based swarm routing all slip with it. The roadmap also says GOVERNS remains in `observe` mode until a 100-clean-pass streak, but does not say whether that streak is required for the launch claim or achievable by October 31. Separately, “P0 items from the three-lens review” is not an actionable gate until the specific open findings and acceptance criteria are enumerated. I could not verify live status or comments on #1515 because GitHub was unreachable, so those may have changed since the roadmap was written.

**Recommendation:** Approve the dependency direction, but treat the four-week date as at risk until Week 1 has named owners, measurable exit criteria, and a fallback scope. Track #1926 and #1993 as the primary schedule risks; decide explicitly whether GOVERNS hardening is required for preview or whether the release will disclose observe mode. Limit the launch claims to evidence actually gathered: calibrated harnesses, measured local-model contribution, one domain-pack pathway, and one successful swarm trial. If those conditions cannot be met, ship a narrower preview or move the date rather than imply unverified capability. **My position is conditional approval of the sequencing, with no unconditional approval of the October 31 release commitment: #1926’s completion and explicit release gates are blocking risks.**

I'll read the revised roadmap and the constraints it depends on, then give a clear approve-or-block recommendation on the four-week sequence.The dependency order is the right topology. Week 1 (stale-goal reconciliation, #1926 state.db consolidation, three-lens P0 security, and the #2136 job-status fix) correctly sits in front of measurement. Landing job-status reconciliation before the Week 2 dispatch waves protects pillar 3: false-negative statuses would poison the capability and cost numbers that pillar exists to produce. Parking distribution work, semantic graphs, and enterprise sync matches #1515's scope clause. Scoping pillar 6 to one domain pack, and keeping deploy on the Claude default unless the Infra role clears five merged samples, are the two places this roadmap already prefers an honest claim over a slipped date.

The calendar does not fit that order. From 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-31 is 21 days, so Week 4 is the release date rather than a build week. The critical path has no float: #1926 (11,000+ shards) → #1993 → the #1937 cost re-investigation → Hermes measurement and the #2102/#2104 soaks → a swarm that picks harnesses by measured fit → changelog, version, blog, and README check. A slip in #1926 pushes every quantitative pillar past the gate.

Three proof bars cannot finish in the slots assigned. Pillar 2, autonomous GOVERNS, is still in observe mode behind a 100-clean-pass streak and has no scheduled week. A streak is elapsed time. Pillar 1's Muse batch and pillar 4's "20% contributor" both need at least five completed and merged jobs under the empirical policy. Samples started in Week 2 or Week 3 will still be in review on 31 October. A 20% routing quota is demonstrable in that window; a 20% measured share of merged work is not. Pillar 5 stays practiced and unmeasured, so it cannot be a release gate.

I approve the sequencing and the dependency order. I do not approve the claim that all seven pillars clear the 2026-10-31 gate at the stated proof level. The blocking risk is real: #1926 is a single point of failure, GOVERNS autonomy is unscheduled, and the Muse and Hermes sample bars outrun the calendar. Hold 31 October only by writing the re-park triggers now. If #1926 is not queryable at the end of Week 1, ship the narrower preview — job-status fix, P0 security, one domain pack, one swarm on existing primitives — with the capability report and the 20% Hermes result still in measurement, GOVERNS still in observe, and deploy still Claude-default. Move the full seven-pillar proof to the next named release.

synthesis: Decision: Approve the sequencing and dependency ordering as drafted — the Week 1 foundation-first gate (#1926 state.db consolidation, #2136 job-status fix, three-lens P0s) ahead of measurement (Week 2), measurement ahead of claims (Week 3), and claims ahead of swarm/release (Week 4) is the correct topology, and all five panelists converge on that. But approval is conditional, not unconditional, on the 2026-10-31 date itself: the panel unanimously flags that #1926 is a single point of failure with no float in a 21-day window, and that the Empirical Capability Assessment Policy's own ≥5-merged-job sample bar makes "measured 20% Hermes contributor," Muse calibration, and GOVERNS exiting observe mode genuinely hard to clear honestly by the 31st — not because the plan is wrong, but because proof-by-merged-sample takes wall-clock time the calendar doesn't have. Adopt two concrete gates rather than relitigating the sequence: (1) an end-of-Week-1 checkpoint — if #1926 is not queryable and #2136 not merged, invoke the re-park trigger immediately rather than letting slip cascade silently through Weeks 2–4; (2) an end-of-Week-2 go/no-go on the local-model and capability-matrix pillars specifically — if sample counts aren't trending toward 5 merged jobs by then, descope those pillars from "measured" to "integrated, unmeasured" in the dev-preview release claims, and explicitly decide (and state in the release notes) whether GOVERNS ships in observe mode rather than letting that become an implicit, undisclosed scope cut. Ship the narrower, honestly-labeled preview over a seven-pillar claim the evidence can't yet support by 10/31.
